thread:
maria: Heads-up: backup-audit flagged ~600 snapshot objects that are SSE-KMS but point to a CMK in state 'PendingDeletion'. Bucket redwood-db-snapshots prefix snapshots/2026-09-10/
security-bot: [alert] kms:key-pending-deletion-referenced - detected references to pending CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:0123456789:key/old-scheduled-cmk (alert ID AS-2026-PLK). https://alerts.redwood.internal/AS-2026-PLK
aj: whoa. Can you paste one HEAD that shows the x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id? need to confirm it's the same key.
maria: sample HEAD output:
```
Content-Length: 536870912
x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms
x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:0123456789:key/old-scheduled-cmk
x-amz-meta-origin: backup-service
```
luca: that key was scheduled for deletion by the key-rotation team last week (ticket KR-2026-77). Deletion date is 2026-10-02T04:00Z. If it gets deleted, any objects encrypted to that CMK may be unrecoverable unless we rewrap while the key is recoverable.
raj-iam: checking KMS console: key state = PendingDeletion, pending window = 30 days, deletion scheduled 2026-10-02. We can cancel deletion using aws kms cancel-key-deletion while the window is open.
kevin-security: How did snapshots end up encrypted with that CMK? current policy says uploader should use alias/redwood-cmk. Was there a migration job that targeted old CMK?\nmaria: there was an archival migration job run 2026-09-10 02:12Z that re-wrapped older snapshots to comply with rotation; looks like it incorrectly used env var KMS_KEY_ID=old-scheduled-cmk in the cron job. PR #backend/archiver 701 referenced a fallback behavior.
aj: I can pull job logs. Quick grep shows the archiver invoked `s3 cp --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:0123456789:key/old-scheduled-cmk` for ~612 objects.
maria: severity P1 due to potential permanent data loss if key deletion completes. Immediate actions?
sam-oncall: immediate: 1) cancel deletion for old-scheduled-cmk (raj), 2) revoke archiver job or update env to point to alias/redwood-cmk (luca), 3) generate list of affected object keys and tenant mapping (aj), 4) notify compliance/legal (erin).
raj-iam: cancelling deletion now. Command I ran:
```
aws kms cancel-key-deletion --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:0123456789:key/old-scheduled-cmk
```
Response: Deletion cancelled. Key state -> Enabled.
kevin-security: Good. Next, we need to rewrap objects to the canonical CMK and prove integrity. How fast can we run a rewrap job for 600 objects?
luca: we can do in-place re-wrap by copying each object with `--metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/redwood-cmk`. For multipart objects use multipart-copy. I'll prepare a parallel worker to avoid hitting rate limits.
aj: I'll produce CSV: object_key,size,put_timestamp,original_uploader,tenant_id. Uploading to incident doc now.
maria: compliance: erin, any regulatory constraints on notifying customers? This was internal re-encryption but if tenants' snapshots temporarily used a non-approved CMK we may need to report.
erin: I'm triaging contracts now. If any tenant has requirements to use customer-managed keys or explicit CMK ARNs, we need to check. For most standard customers this is an internal key choice; still, we'll include the timeline and mitigation in a notification packet.
kevin-security: post-containment controls:
  - add a pre-deploy lint that blocks archiver jobs referencing key ARNs not in allowed list (aliases: alias/redwood-cmk, alias/retention-cmk)
  - require KMS key-id env vars to be validated by CI against a whitelist
  - add Athena query + alert for any PutObject/CopyObject where x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id matches keys in PendingDeletion state
  - update runbook to auto-cancel deletion if referenced by snapshot objects

luca: hotfix: patched archiver cron to use alias/redwood-cmk and added a guard to abort if KMS_KEY_ID resolves to a key in PendingDeletion. Deploying now.
sam-oncall: I'll throttle the rewrap job to avoid hitting KMS CreateGrant limits and monitor API errors. Also will coordinate with infra to increase concurrent copy workers if needed.
aj: CSV with 612 keys uploaded to incident page: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-KEYWRAP. Starting checksum verification on a 10-object sample copy to alias/redwood-cmk.
luca: rewrap dry-run completed for sample; verified ETag and content-length parity for single-part objects. Multipart copy requires recompute validation but process working.
raj-iam: also auditing who scheduled deletion - key-rotation team. Adding a guard: key rotation deletes must check for active references in S3 metadata (via Athena) before scheduling deletion. I'll open a follow-up ticket.
maria: timeline for status update to exec/cs/legal in 2 hours. erin please prepare templates. kevin, include recommended permanent controls and detection rules.
erin: will prepare notification draft and escalate to legal if any contract hit. Notifying CS for customers with restores in flight.
security-bot: Incident created INC-2026-KEYWRAP severity=P1 responders=@maria @aj @luca @sam-oncall @erin @raj-iam @kevin-security
maria: thanks all — primary risk mitigated by cancelling deletion. Keep rewrap progress and any failures in the incident doc. We'll schedule a postmortem and update the KMS deletion checklist. :thumbsup:"
